in_urdu.name: سدری
in_urdu.long_meaning: جنت میں سے احدین من مفقودوں سے، وہ برکتوں کے ساتھ باہر ہونے والے ہیں اور جس لئے وہ در سے متاونا ہیں। انہیں من مفقودوں میں سے ہوتے ہیں جس کے ساتھ باہری اور علم کا فراغ ملائی جاتا ہوا.

in_hindi.name: सद्री
in_hindi.long_meaning: जनती में से एक सिखाया था जो دर से छोड़ा था। वह जن्तुओं से बाहर होकर सर्वसाधनी विद्या प्राप्त कर सकते थे।

in_pashto.name: سدري
in_pashto.long_meaning: در ستانه در محفوظ راحت سوار ہونده اور سب طرف سے مفقود علم برکتوں سے باہر ہوئے ہیں.

in_english.name: Sadri
in_english.meaning: One who is devoid of knowledge

The name signifies one who is content and pleased, and has a bright and cheerful disposition. It is a touching tribute to the traditional Islamic values of contentment, gratitude, and inner peace.

It inspires us to cultivate inner peace, gratitude, and contentment, and to remain focused on the blessings of God, rather than on material possessions or circumstances beyond our control. The name "Sadri" also reflects the deep faith that a true believer should have in Allah's infinite wisdom and mercy, and the understanding that true happiness and blessing come from within. Ultimately, the name "Sadri" is a shining example of the transformative power of faith and inner peace, and a reminder to strive towards these noble qualities in our daily lives.

historical_references.reference: Sultan Sadr al-Din Muhammad Shah, also known as Sultan Muhammad bin Tughluq, ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1320 to 1351 AD. He is known for his ambitious plans, one of which was to move his capital from Delhi to Hosangabad, in the Deccan region. This venture failed due to logistical challenges.

Sheikh Sadruddin Auliya, a Sufi saint, was born in 1177 AD in Afghanistan. He spent most of his life in India, especially in the city of Delhi, and is considered to be one of the most significant figures of the Chishti Sufi order. He is particularly famous for his teachings on love and compassion.
